draft_key_information_units.information: The Group reported strong headline financial performance in 2025 with total revenue of EUR 53.2 million (2024: EUR 18.2 million), gross profit of EUR 18.8 million (35% margin, 2024: EUR 5.4 million, 30%), operating profit of EUR 14.7 million (2024: EUR 0.1 million), net profit of EUR 12.0 million (2024: EUR 3.9 million loss), earnings per share of EUR 0.22 (2024: EUR -0.06), and operating cash flow generating EUR 10.8 million (2024: EUR 10.4 million used). Total assets increased to EUR 124,490 thousand (2024: EUR 118,758 thousand), total equity rose to EUR 63,327 thousand (2024: EUR 51,221 thousand), with cash of EUR 5,143 thousand (2024: EUR 4,344 thousand), net asset value per share of EUR 1.12 (2024: EUR 0.89), and debt-to-equity ratio improving to 0.97 (2024: 1.32).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report - Key financials; Key performance indicators table; Consolidated interim statements of comprehensive income and financial position

draft_key_information_units.information: Revenue growth was primarily driven by the handover of completed residential units in the Kalaranna District and Uus-Kindrali developments in Tallinn, as well as the City Villas project in Vilnius, contrasting lower 2024 revenue due to delayed starts in Kalaranna and limited sales elsewhere.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report - Revenue from real estate sales section

draft_key_information_units.information: Segmental revenue shifted significantly, with Estonia contributing 75% of total revenue in 2025 (versus 27% in 2024), Latvia's contribution falling to 0.3% (from 25%), and Lithuania maintaining a stable 12% share (versus 11% in 2024).

Liquidity and capital position improved, reflected in a reduced debt-to-equity ratio of 0.97 (2024: 1.32) and increased net asset value per share to EUR 1.12 (2024: EUR 0.89), supported by active management of bank loans and bonds.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key performance indicators table; Financing sources and policies section

draft_key_information_units.information: Major real estate developments advanced: completion of the white building in Uus-Kindrali (Tallinn) with 39 units closed by year-end (78% of sellable area sold); construction commenced on the Blue Marine project in Riga's Klīversala Quarter; first real rights agreements signed and units handed over in Šaltinių Namai Attico (Vilnius); and building permit obtained for the Borgo luxury residential complex in Vilnius (construction planned for H2 2026).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Chairman’s summary; Overview of the development projects section

draft_key_information_units.information: Hotel operations performed slightly below budget for the full year 2025, with occupancy levels softening towards year-end, though food and beverage revenue increased modestly year-on-year. Italian operations (Preatoni Nuda Proprietà and Preatoni Intermediazioni Immobiliari) faced a challenging market with subdued transaction volumes.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Hotel operations section; Other operations section

draft_key_information_units.information: The Group acquired an additional 10% stake in Preatoni Nuda Proprietà S.r.l. in September 2025, increasing its ownership to 77.5%, and recognized a full impairment loss of EUR 863 thousand on the associated goodwill due to revised profitability projections and financing dependencies.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Note 4 - Business combination; Note 5 - Partly-owned subsidiaries

draft_key_information_units.information: The Group amended terms of its senior secured callable fixed-rate bonds (ISIN SE0013801172) in February 2025, partially repaid EUR 9.405 million in August 2025, reducing outstanding nominal amount to EUR 10.545 million, and managed bank loan repayments and new borrowings to maintain financing flexibility.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Main events section; Financing sources and policies section; Note 11 - Current and non-current debt

evaluation.selection_rationale: The draft units focus on material summary-level content directly supporting concise financial-report evaluation: headline financial performance (D1), major revenue drivers (D2), segmental shifts (D3), liquidity/capital position (D4), key project developments (D5), operational performance in hotels and Italy (D6), strategic acquisition and impairment (D7), and financing activities (D8). All units are factually supported by the source report, avoid boilerplate, and represent independently omittable themes. Priority was given to HIGH-importance items central to financial performance, drivers, liquidity, and strategy, with one MEDIUM unit (D3 and D6) included for material relevance. The selection aligns with the reference summary and source structure, limiting coverage to approximately 8 units within the 6–10 target range.
